title: When the Mixtape Sings
premise: In the fading mill town of Halloway, Ivo Eriksen has survived high school by being unremarkable — except for being its only out kid. When notes begin appearing in his locker, written in ink that shifts color and vanishes by morning, he learns they come from the school's legendary ghost: a student who died in a 1987 fire the school board ruled an accident. The ghost's messages lead Ivo to evidence that the fire was arson, covered up to protect the town's founding family, whose descendants still sit on the school board. As the board moves to demolish the old wing and bury the truth forever, Ivo must choose between staying invisible and going public, knowing the same machinery that silenced a kid in 1987 can silence him too. In the end, Ivo broadcasts the ghost's testimony over the school's ancient PA system during graduation rehearsal, forcing an investigation — but justice comes at a cost: the ghost finally fades, and Ivo loses the one person who ever truly saw him.
about_author: Lena Eastwick grew up in a shuttered mill town in the Pacific Northwest, where she spent more afternoons than she'll admit exploring condemned school buildings. She writes queer small-town gothics for teens who know that some ghosts are just truths nobody wanted buried with them.

chapters.title: Fine
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A routine day at Halloway High establishes his careful invisibility: the jokes he laughs off, the best friend who doesn't quite get it, the town's nine hundred watchful eyes. Emotional beat: weary self-containment, the performance of 'fine.' Ends with him finding the first note in his locker — his name, in ink that shimmers like oil on water.

chapters.title: The Legend of Wing B
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He researches the school ghost story: Danny Voss, class of 1988, died when the old music wing burned the night of the winter concert. Everyone knows the legend; no one questions it. Emotional beat: skeptical curiosity curdling into unease when he realizes the note's handwriting matches Danny's yearbook signature exactly.

chapters.title: Impossible Ink
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A second note appears inside his locked car, describing something only Ivo knows — a secret he's told no one. He tests the ink: it vanishes at dawn, leaves no residue, and is cold to the touch. Emotional beat: terror warring with a desperate, shameful hope that someone, finally, sees him.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Witnesses
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Priya Chandrasekaran, the school paper editor and Ivo's reluctant ally-in-observation. She's noticed the board fast-tracking demolition permits for Wing B. Emotional beat: the chapter widens the lens — Halloway as a town built on looking away — while Ivo realizes someone else has been asking questions too.

chapters.title: What the Notes Ask
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The notes stop being cryptic and become instructions: find the 1987 concert program; check the fire marshal's report. Each request costs him — sneaking into the records room means risking detention, and worse, visibility. Emotional beat: complicity deepening; he's no longer a recipient but a participant.

chapters.title: The Ashwell Name
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She traces the school board: three of five members are Ashwells or married to Ashwells, the family that owned the mill and funded the school. Her own mother warns her off the story. Emotional beat: first taste of how power operates here — not with threats, but with polite, smiling pressure.

chapters.title: Detention with the Dead
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Caught in Wing B after hours, Ivo serves detention repainting the gym — and meets the ghost face to face among the bleachers: Danny, seventeen forever, flickering like a bad film print. Emotional beat: fear dissolving into grief; Danny isn't haunting the school, he's trapped in it.

chapters.title: The Night It Burned
chapters.summary: Danny's POV — the novel's first full ghost chapter. Flashback to December 1987: Danny found the Ashwell heir's ledger proving embezzled construction funds, planned to hand it to the newspaper, and was locked in the music wing before the fire started. Emotional beat: betrayal and terror rendered intimate; the reader now knows what Ivo only suspects.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine (A Lie, Repeated)
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. His best friend Marcus confronts him about his secrecy, and their friendship fractures — Marcus can't follow Ivo into this, not with a scholarship and an Ashwell recommendation letter pending. Emotional beat: the price of the truth begins coming due in ordinary currency.

chapters.title: Ledger Lines
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Following Danny's clues, she and Ivo locate a copy of the ledger hidden in the time capsule under the flagpole — along with a 1988 police statement that was never filed. Emotional beat: triumph that immediately sours; the statement names names, including the current board chair's father.

chapters.title: The Polite Meeting
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Board Chair Eleanor Ashwell invites Ivo to her office — all warmth and concern — and offers him a college fund, a fresh start anywhere he likes, if he'd simply return some 'misplaced historical documents.' Emotional beat: corruption wearing its Sunday best; Ivo understands he's being bought, and that refusal has a shape he doesn't want to learn.

chapters.title: Vanishing Act
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The time capsule contents disappear from the newspaper office overnight; the faculty advisor kills Priya's story; her mother receives a call from the mill's successor company. Emotional beat: the machinery of cover-up grinding into motion, quiet and total — power doesn't rage, it tidies.

chapters.title: Demolition Day Is Set
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The board announces Wing B will come down before graduation — 'a gift to the class of tomorrow.' Danny begins to fade as the building is scheduled for destruction, his existence tied to it. Emotional beat: a ticking clock made flesh; saving the truth now means saving Danny, and there may be no way to do both.

chapters.title: What Ghosts Keep
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. Danny shows Ivo where he hid the original ledger and a cassette tape — his own voice, recorded the night he died, naming the Ashwell heir as the arsonist. But taking it means breaking the seal on the old band room, which Danny warns will end whatever is keeping him here. Emotional beat: love expressed as warning; sacrifice offered without being asked.

chapters.title: The Band Room Seal
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo refuses to take the tape if it kills Danny; they fight — the living boy and the dead one — about who gets to be brave. Emotional beat: the central moral knot tightened: justice for Danny versus Danny himself. Ends with Ivo stealing the key alone, unable to choose.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds of Static
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya recovers a partial copy of the fire marshal's report from a retired marshal's estate sale and discovers the original investigation was closed from above within forty-eight hours. Emotional beat: validation and fury — the system didn't fail Danny; it worked exactly as designed.

chapters.title: Graduation Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The whole senior class gathers in the gym while workers begin stripping Wing B next door. Danny is nearly transparent now, visible only to Ivo. Eleanor Ashwell takes the podium to announce the memorial plaque — 'in loving memory' language that erases everything. Emotional beat: the moment before detonation; Ivo has the cassette in his jacket and the PA room key in his pocket.

chapters.title: When the Mixtape Sings
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, climax. During the rehearsal, Ivo locks himself in the AV booth and plays Danny's tape over every speaker in the school — Danny's voice naming his killer, the ledger numbers read aloud, thirty-eight years of silence broken in front of nine hundred students. Eleanor Ashwell's composure cracks on camera as phones record everything. Emotional beat: catharsis through exposure; the invisible kid makes the whole town listen.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Loud and Clear
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Consequences cascade: state investigators arrive, the demolition halts, the Ashwell heir — now a judge — resigns quietly. But Ivo faces expulsion hearings and a town split between gratitude and resentment. Emotional beat: justice outside the law arrives messy, incomplete, and real; victory tastes like ash and oxygen both.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At his disciplinary hearing, students — led by a changed Marcus — pack the room and refuse to disperse until charges are dropped. The board, gutted by scandal, folds. Emotional beat: solidarity as redemption; the boy who was alone in chapter one stands in a crowd that chose him.

chapters.title: Last Bell
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. With the building saved and the truth public, Danny's tether releases. Their goodbye happens in the restored band room at dusk: no drama, just two boys talking about music and what might have been, until the ink of Danny's final note — 'thank you for hearing me' — fades for the last time. Emotional beat: grief braided with peace; being seen was worth every cost.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, epilogue. One year later: Wing B reopens as a community arts center with Danny Voss's name on the door and his story in the curriculum. Ivo, bound for college out east, leaves a note of his own in the band room — addressed to whoever needs it next. Emotional beat: inheritance and forward motion; the mixtape keeps singing because someone finally passed it on.
